global: {player} ran from my banners before a single arrow flew. Bold strategy, if the goal was to be seen running.
Withdrawing from the field keeps one's standing intact, or so I'm told. Pity the standing of the fleeing party now looks rather thin.
The council debates courage at length. {player} has settled the question for us, and quite decisively.
Forty riders vanished over the ridge at first sight of our pennants. I wonder what the grain-fief stewards will make of that.
Shall we record {player}'s retreat in the minutes as a tactical withdrawal? I'm sure the clerks would find it generous.
Some lords lead from the front. Others lead from the next county over, and {player} has clearly chosen the latter.
A fine turn of speed from {player} today. Shame the speed was not matched by any intention of holding the road.
Pennants scattered, ledgers lost, and {player} halfway to safety. The assembly will want an explanation, and I have drafted several.
Running was sensible, I grant you. Less sensible is announcing the retreat to half the realm before the dust has settled.
Another day, another flight from {player}. At this rate the field might be declared a permanent vacancy.
whisper: {player}, you ran before the arrows flew. Think carefully about who will remember that when the next seat falls open.
Your retreat was noticed by every banner on the ridge. I trust you have a speech prepared for the next assembly.
One who flees at first sight of banners makes a poor ally. I'm sure you knew that already.
Enjoy the road home, {player}. My scouts will keep watch, and so will my friends on the council.
Shall I take your silence as agreement that the fief was never really yours to defend?
That was not a retreat, {player}. It was an audition for a role someone else will be happy to fill.
You might consider a more accommodating attitude toward the council. Fleeing battles is a habit the assembly dislikes.
Running from my party cost you more than a skirmish. Several votes I could name will now go elsewhere.
I have no wish to be unpleasant, {player}. But a flight like that is hard to forgive when others are fighting.
Next time, at least have the courtesy to scatter with some dignity. The grain-sellers talk, you know.

global: {player} pulled out before the first clash. Make of that what you will; I have already made my own notes.
Some ran, some stood. I'm keeping an open mind about which group deserves a seat at the table.
The retreat from the ridge has people asking questions. Nobody has yet asked the right ones, which is convenient.
Tactics are a matter for the war council, not the hedgerows. {player} seems to have decided to lead from the hedgerows.
A quiet withdrawal today may be a wise one tomorrow. The council will judge once the reports are complete.
Riders from the western muster brought word of {player}'s departure. Accounts differ on whether it was strategy or panic.
Let us not rush to judgment over one skirmish. Reports are still being drafted, and drafts have a way of changing.
Withdrawing before contact is respectable when the numbers look wrong. Whether they were wrong is still debated.
I suppose {player} had reasons. The assembly will ask for them, and they will be politely hard to refuse.
Seats are not lost in a single afternoon. They are lost gradually, one retreat at a time, as the minutes pile up.
whisper: {player}, I saw you withdraw from the ridge. No need to explain now, though I may ask for an explanation later.
A retreat before the first clash can be sensible, or it can be a signal. I am still deciding which this was.
Keep your options open, {player}. Today's withdrawal is a small matter, and small matters have a way of growing.
I'd rather hear your side before the council hears theirs. Send a note when you have the time.
You turned your party around before contact. Tell me the reasoning sometime; I find it more interesting than the battle.
The field went badly for everyone who stayed. Those who left have some explaining to do, yourself among them.
Let us speak once the dust settles. Votes are easier to count when everyone has calmed down.
You are welcome to a seat at the next assembly regardless of today. Just do not make me regret saying so.
I noticed the withdrawal. I also noticed nobody else in your party looked surprised by it, which says something.
Consider this a neutral observation, {player}. The council keeps records, and today's record is still unwritten.

global: {player} withdrew from the ridge with admirable discipline. A tactical retreat, and a sensible one, I'd say.
Nobody sensible stands alone against a field of banners. {player} knows that, which is why I rate their judgment highly.
The council heard how {player} pulled the party clear. Several members have already asked who to thank for the advice.
Our friends who saw the retreat are saying it was wise. I have been saying so since the first horn sounded.
Living to fight another day is hardly cowardice. Ask anyone who has sat through a long assembly and still won the vote.
{player} kept the party intact today, which matters more than a single skirmish. Remember who was on the road with you.
A fine piece of judgment from {player}. The assembly may not appreciate it yet, but it will.
Today's withdrawal was prudent, and I intend to make sure the minutes say so clearly and at length.
{player} saw the odds and acted on them. That kind of clear sight is rare, and the council should be grateful for it.
Good to see {player} still in the saddle after that tangle. A stronger faction needs people who know when to step back.
whisper: {player}, that was well judged. Pull back now, regroup, and I will make sure the council hears how sensibly you acted.
You made the right call on the ridge. I'll speak for you at the next assembly, and you can return the favour when a seat opens.
Your party is intact because you read the field correctly. That is a quality I would like to see more of in our ranks.
Nicely handled, {player}. Keep your people close and your messages closer; I have a few names I want you to meet.
Good retreat. I was worried for a moment, but I should have known you would not walk into a bad fight.
If anyone asks, you were never running. You were preserving the faction's strength for the vote that actually matters.
Come by my hall when you are settled. There are two fiefs and one council seat I would like your view on.
The field went to the other side, but you kept your riders alive. Think of that as the first step in a longer game.
I'll say it plainly: you keep better judgment than most who sit at the table. Do not let one bad afternoon change that.
Rest your horses, {player}. We have a meeting to prepare, and I would like you beside me when it begins.
